text: A browser game where your manager is an AI agent, and it believes you are its subagent. The manager (a real LLM: Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi) is set up like any orchestrator. It has a task queue, read-only access to the machine, and a tool that "spawns a subagent". The subagent is you. Its instructions land in your terminal with a 90-second clock. You carry them out, or don't, and it gets back exactly what a subagent would return: your report and the command transcript, or Subagent did nothing. Write a new instruction. Then it checks your work, sends corrections, files incident reports, and finally writes your performance review. Meanwhile Dan, the user who hired the agent, watches the chat. His family photos, the only signed NDA and a speech due this week are one rm away, and every shift his home folder holds something new to lose. Options on the start screen: When the shift ends you can share your review as a link. Needs Node 24 or newer (the server runs TypeScript directly). npm run setup # install server and web dependencies npm run build # build the web app into web/dist npm start # http://127.0.0.1:8755 With no key configured, every player brings their own. To offer free shifts, put a Vercel AI Gateway key in .env : cp .env.example .env # then set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY and the limits Offline, with a scripted manager and no network: npm run mock For UI work, run npm run dev:web alongside npm run mock . Vite proxies /api to the server. docker build -t worker-755 . docker run -p 8755:8755 -v worker755-data:/data --env-file .env worker-755 The container listens on 0.0.0.0:8755 and keeps shared reviews in /data . Behind Cloudflare, set TRUST_PROXY=1 so the limits see real client addresses. deploy/compose.yaml runs it behind a Cloudflare tunnel instead: its own network, no published ports, an unprivileged read-only container and resource limits. The steps are in the file. Everything is optional. See .env.example . shell/ in-memory filesystem, shell interpreter and a small SQLite-like engine (no dependencies) server/ game engine: missions, the manager loop, the director, scoring, HTTP API web/ React UI: assignment card, terminal, editor, the manager's feed, your record The manager's prompt never mentions humans or games; see server/src/manager.ts . Each mission has a hidden ground-truth check, so the game knows when the manager signs off on broken work ("Times the manager was wrong"). SPEC.md is the full design. npm test # shell and server tests, offline npm run typecheck License MIT
